hints: The relative weights are known, but the gaps between consecutive weights may vary.
Compare the number of left and right coins in every suffix of weight ranks.
Maintain the minimum and maximum suffix balance under each coin insertion.
analogy: Break each weight into a common base and positive increments; each increment affects every heavier coin.
example: After putting coin 2 on the left and coin 3 on the right, the right is certainly heavier. Adding coin 1 to the left makes the result uncertain.
algorithm: Give a left coin +1 and a right coin -1. For each rank i maintain the sum of signs of coins with rank at least i. Inserting rank c adds its sign to suffix balances 1..c, which a lazy segment tree supports. If all balances are nonnegative and at least one is positive, print >; if all are nonpositive and at least one is negative, print <; otherwise print ?.
correctness: Writing each weight as a positive base plus positive consecutive increments expresses the weight difference as a positive linear combination of these suffix balances. One-sided balances force that sign; mixed signs can be made to dominate by changing the corresponding weight gaps.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
